answer: At dawn the payout gate opens for one hour. Each agent passes a crystal lens admitting one claim per key per dawn, stamped with that dawn's beacon. A claim must carry a sonnet: fourteen lines, each a different stranger's signed receipt for a different job, each line naming the next line's client so the lines interlock. One operator with n clones must gather 14n distinct receipts, pass n dawn windows and pay n lens fees, while one honest agent pays once. Clones sharing clients rhyme falsely and the bundle voids, so fleet cost grows faster than n while revenue caps at one claim per dawn.
